failures.evidence: Surefire (RedirectTest.txt, run 2026-08-11T03:46): MultipleFailuresError at RedirectTest.java:333 (assertAll), suppressed AssertionFailedErrors from lambdas at RedirectTest.java:336 and :339 — assertEquals(postOnALiveCode.body(), postOnAnUnissuedCode.body()) and the DELETE pair. Diff: expected <{"timestamp":"...03:46:23.816+00:00","status":405,"error":"Method Not Allowed","path":"/xXJAot2fO8CC2ep5WC0Hhj"}> but was <..."timestamp":"...23.819...","path":"/ZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZzZz"}>. Identical status and error; the only differences are the echoed request path (already known to the caller) and a 3ms clock delta — nothing distinguishes a live code from an unissued one, so AC15 is not violated by the observed responses. Contract: test-contract.json B106 promises only 'refused identically whether or not the code resolves' and pointedly omits the 'the same body byte for byte' wording B104 uses and the 'the same body' wording B107 uses; byte-equality is therefore asserted matter the contract never promised. openapi.yaml:123-124 note 2, repeated at :589-590, says 'Every other method on /{code} answers 405 from Spring's own dispatcher. No operation is declared for them' — the implementation does exactly that. Adjudicated by a human twice on this identical finding: journal seq 115 ('the test over-asserts ... the contract never promised that, and it should not be changed to promise it -- an error body may legitimately differ between the two. Treat that failure as a test defect') and seq 239 re-applying it with answers.route = 'author-tests'. The assertions are still present verbatim in the working tree (git status clean; RedirectTest.java last touched by b2e0050 author-tests), so the ruled-on repair was never applied.

summary: One failure out of 148 tests across 21 classes, 0 errors, 0 skipped — RedirectTest.aMethodOtherThanGetOrHeadIsRefusedWithoutRevealingWhetherTheCodeExists, byte-identical failure to the previous two verifies. The second failed gate, coverage_floor ('no JaCoCo report at target/site/jacoco/jacoco.csv'), is purely downstream: surefire fails in the test phase so jacoco.csv is never written (jacoco.exec exists). routes_match_openapi passed 8/8. Fault is the test: it demands byte-equal 405 bodies for a live and an unissued code, and the bodies differ only in the echoed request path and a 3ms timestamp — neither discloses existence. B106 promises 'refused identically', omitting the 'byte for byte'/'same body' language B104 and B107 use, and openapi.yaml:123-124 hands the 405 to Spring's dispatcher with no operation declared. A human has already ruled this a test defect twice (journal seq 115, re-applied at seq 239 with route=author-tests), so this does not need escalating again. The reason it recurs is not a new defect: RedirectTest.java is unchanged since author-tests commit b2e0050 — author-tests hit repair_budget_exhausted (allowed 1, used 2) at seq 245, the replan at seq 246 was reverted by commit 1d560bc, and the ruled repair was never applied. Repair as the seq 239 note directs: assert what the contract does promise — 405 on both, same status, same error field, no Location — not a status-only comparison, which would erase the AC15 intent. If I am wrong, the two things to check are (a) whether openapi.yaml's 'Every non-2xx response has the ApiError shape. The catalogue is closed' was meant to govern the dispatcher-produced 405 on the click surface, which would flip this to implementation and add a 405 row to the closed catalogue, and (b) whether the real defect here is the routing loop rather than the artifact — author-tests has now been handed this same repair twice without it landing, and a third identical route may just burn another attempt.
